trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumakuru, M.C.No.222/2015
case_name: Mrs E Nagamani vs Mr Venkatesh T G
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2013. No children were born. The husband claimed the wife stayed with him for only 3 months and then left. He also alleged cruelty by the wife. The wife wanted a separate house and a lavish lifestyle. The husband's father was suffering from cancer, and he couldn't stay away from his parents.

legal_principles.principle: Pleadings relating to cruelty and desertion must specify particular instances of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The pleading relating to the alleged cruelty does not make reference to any specific instances of cruelty. The evidence also does not make any reference to specific instances of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for restitution of conjugal rights passed exparte cannot be used to prove desertion.
legal_principles.held: Merely because there is a decree for restitution of conjugal rights in favour of the husband, which is passed exparte, it cannot be said that wife has deserted the company of the husband.

legal_principles.principle: The Family Court must follow well-settled principles governing pleading and proof of cruelty and desertion.
legal_principles.held: This court has considered the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the wife. We have considered the pleadings as well as the evidence placed on record with reference to well established principles governing pleading and proof of cruelty and desertion under the Act of 1955.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is filed under Section 19(1) of the Family Courts Act, 1984. The judgment and decree dated 18.01.2017 passed in M.C.No.222/2015 are set aside.
